english: Let $P$ and $Q$ be distinct points on the ellipse $\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{4}=1$ such that the chord $PQ$ is parallel to the line $x+2\sqrt{3}\,y=0$. Let $O$ be the origin. Then the minimum value of $\overrightarrow{OP}\cdot\overrightarrow{OQ}$, taken over all such chords $PQ$, is
hindi: माना कि दीर्घवृत्त $\dfrac{x^{2}}{16}+\dfrac{y^{2}}{4}=1$ पर $P$ तथा $Q$ ऐसे भिन्न बिन्दु हैं कि जीवा $PQ$ रेखा $x+2\sqrt{3}\,y=0$ के समान्तर है। माना $O$ मूलबिन्दु है। तब ऐसी सभी जीवाओं $PQ$ पर $\overrightarrow{OP}\cdot\overrightarrow{OQ}$ का न्यूनतम मान है
solution: Minimum at $\alpha-\beta=\pi$ ($P,Q$ ends of a diameter, e.g. $\alpha=\dfrac{5\pi}{6},\ \beta=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$): $-10-3=-13$
solution_full: The line $x+2\sqrt3\,y=0$ has slope $-\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt3}$. Equating, $\cot\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2}=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$, so $\dfrac{\alpha+\beta}{2}=\dfrac{\pi}{3}+k\pi$ and $\alpha+\beta=\dfrac{2\pi}{3}+2k\pi$. In every case $\cos(\alpha+\beta)=-\dfrac12$.

The constraint fixes only $\alpha+\beta$; $\alpha-\beta$ can take any value with $\alpha\ne\beta$. The minimum $-13$ occurs at $\alpha-\beta=\pi$, for example $\alpha=\dfrac{5\pi}{6}$, $\beta=-\dfrac{\pi}{6}$, giving $P(-2\sqrt3,1)$, $Q(2\sqrt3,-1)$; then $\overrightarrow{OP}\cdot\overrightarrow{OQ}=-12-1=-13$.
Option (B) $-a^{2}$ would need the diameter along the major axis, which is not parallel to the given line; (C) and (D) drop or mis-sign the $6\cos(\alpha+\beta)$ term.
originality_note: New: the extreme of OP.OQ over a family of parallel chords, where the chord direction fixes alpha + beta and the product-to-sum identity separates the free variable alpha - beta (way 5). Closest known: chords in a given direction have constant sum of eccentric angles; maximum area of triangle OPQ. Different because: the quantity is a dot product whose two parts behave differently under the constraint, so the constraint must be decoded first.
stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, point and curve introduced, conditions complete, one reading of each sentence; answer recomputed with sympy and unique; answer matches the plan. Checked that P and Q distinct is stated, that the minimum is attained (a diameter parallel to the line), and numerically over 4000 chords. Changed: No change.
key_step: Decode 'parallel to the line' into cos(alpha + beta) = -1/2, then 10 cos(alpha - beta) - 3.
justification: Two linked ideas: the chord-direction condition on eccentric angles and the extreme of a trigonometric expression under the constraint alpha + beta fixed. Comparable to 2025-P2-Q7 (L3), eccentric-angle reasoning on an ellipse.
blueprint_concepts: Maximum and minimum of general trigonometric expressions under constraints

concept_use.Parametric coordinates for Ellipse: P and Q are written as (4 cos alpha, 2 sin alpha) and (4 cos beta, 2 sin beta); the slope of PQ in eccentric angles gives the condition on alpha + beta.
concept_use.Maximum and minimum of general trigonome: OP.OQ = 10 cos(alpha - beta) + 6 cos(alpha + beta) is minimised under the constraint cos(alpha + beta) = -1/2, giving -13 at alpha - beta = pi.
